title: How to Spot and Block Fake Bank Text Message Alerts
bigPicture: Real companies will not ask for your account information by text, so treat an unexpected text asking for it as a likely scam.
whatYouNeedToKnow: Legitimate companies won't ask for information about your account by text.
Do not click links in an unexpected text that asks for personal or financial information.
If a message might be real, contact the company using a phone number or website you already know is genuine, not the details in the text.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Clicking a link in a text that asks for personal or financial information, even if it looks urgent.
Calling the phone number or opening the website given in the text instead of one you already know is real.
actionSteps: Stop and do not click anything in the text.
Contact your bank using the number on your card, your statement, or the bank's official website.
Forward a copy of the text to 7726 (SPAM). This helps your wireless provider block similar messages.
Use your messaging app's option to report junk or spam.
Report it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

sources.label: FTC: How to recognize and report spam text messages
